question.text: Will the Save Our Bacon Act be enacted into law before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before July 1, 2027, federal legislation is enacted into law that preempts state regulation of out-of-state pork production.

Specifically, the enacted text must establish that pork producers may raise and market their products in interstate commerce, free from state or local production-process standards imposed on pigs physically raised outside the state's borders. The statute may also cover other livestock (e.g., cattle, veal, dairy), but pork coverage is what this question turns on.
question.fine_print:
* Enactment may occur via presidential signature, becoming law without signature, or veto override. The legislation may be a standalone bill or a provision within other legislation such as the Farm Bill, appropriations, or the NDAA.
* Court rulings, executive orders, or USDA rulemakings achieving similar effects do not count.
* A bill that grandfathers existing state laws, applies only prospectively to laws enacted after a certain date, or contains a state opt-out provision will not resolve **Yes**.
* The effective date of the bill does not matter, as long as it is enacted before July 1, 2027.

research:
I couldn't find anything showing that the Save Our Bacon Act, or any Prop 12 preemption, has become law or is about to. Only the House-passed Farm Bill contains the language. The Senate committee's bill leaves it out. Democrats won both chambers on November 3, 2026, and the most-cited Republican compromise in the Senate (Ernst's) would grandfather existing state laws, which would not count for a Yes.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-12: congress.gov returned HTTP 403, so I could not read the H.R. 7567 or H.R. 4673 pages directly. Secondary sources show no enactment. The resolution source is effectively congress.gov's "Became Law" status for any vehicle (Farm Bill, appropriations, NDAA) that carries qualifying pork preemption text.
- 2026-04-30: the House passed H.R. 7567 by 224-200. Section 12006 holds the Save Our Bacon language. [Spotlight PA](https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2026/06/farm-bill-save-our-bacon-act-animal-welfare-state-laws-federal-government/), [National Hog Farmer](https://www.nationalhogfarmer.com/farming-business-management/house-farm-bill-passes-with-prop-12-fix)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The two chambers' bills have not been reconciled, and no conference report exists.
- 2026-09-16: Senate Agriculture advanced its "Agricultural Act of 2026" by 12-11 on party lines, with no Prop 12 fix. Boozman refused to reopen amendments for Sen. Ernst's proposal. That proposal "preserves Proposition 12 and other existing state laws" and blocks only future state rules. That is a grandfather design, which would resolve No even if enacted. [KTVO](https://www.ktvo.com/news/local/senate-agriculture-committee-advances-farm-bill-as-prop-12-debate-moves-to-senate-floor/article_7fa63fb4-8d41-479d-a345-44739e3bd8ee.html)
- Boozman has said he does not think "there's a single Democrat that would vote for" the House provision. The Senate needs 60 votes. [AgDaily](https://www.agdaily.com/news/senate-farm-bill-draft-advances-prop-12-fight-unresolved/)
- Sen. Roger Marshall withdrew as a cosponsor of a Senate version of Save Our Bacon. [The Humane League](https://thehumaneleague.org/article/2026-farm-bill)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-09: DTN reports Congress is back with about 20 legislative days left. Government funding runs out December 11, and only 3 of 12 appropriations bills have cleared the House. SNAP cost-sharing is the "gatekeeper" issue. A farm bill could ride on a CR or omnibus. Democrats may hold out or write their own bill in 2027. [DTN](https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/ag/livestock/article/2026/11/09/farm-bill-competes-crowded-lame-duck)
- 2026-11-09: analysts say the farm bill faces an "uphill battle." One analyst (Mary Kay Thatcher) puts lame-duck odds at "slim to none." [Brownfield](https://brownfieldagnews.com/news/analysts-farm-bill-faces-uphill-battle-in-final-weeks-of-congress/), [AgWeb](https://www.agweb.com/news/senate-farm-bill-scores-4-4-billion-lame-duck-passage-uncertain)
- 2026-11-06: Boozman says a farm bill is still possible by the December 18 adjournment. He lists Prop 12 among unresolved issues alongside SNAP and E15. [Brownfield](https://brownfieldagnews.com/news/boozman-farm-bill-compromise-possible-during-lame-duck-session/)
- 2026-11-05: The New Lede reports Democrats flipped both the House and Senate on November 3, giving them control from January 2027. Industry group AMPA argues Ashley Hinson's support for the bill cost her the Iowa Senate race. [The New Lede](https://www.thenewlede.org/2026/11/midterms-farm-bill-senate/)
- 2026-11-10: Sen. Rick Scott criticized the GOP plan to adjourn and expects Democrats to take both chambers. [Breitbart](https://www.breitbart.com/politics/2026/11/10/exclusive-sen-rick-scott-calls-on-gop-led-senate-to-work-instead-of-going-home-pass-voter-id-confirm-trump-judges/)
- 2026-09-30: the farm bill extension expired. [AgWeb](https://www.agweb.com/news/farm-bill-expires-congress-faces-tight-deadline-renewal)
- 2026-08-06: the first Senate committee vote failed 10-11 over SNAP. [ProAg](https://www.proag.com/news/senate-farm-bill-fails-on-10-11-vote-as-snap-dispute-splits-committee/)

## 4. Base rates
- The King Amendment and its successors have never been enacted. The House included versions in 2013-14 and in the 2018 House farm bill, and both were dropped in conference. The final 2018 farm bill passed in a December lame duck after Democrats had flipped the House, without the King language. [AWI](https://awionline.org/awi-quarterly/2013-fall/king-amendment%E2%80%99s-attack-state-animal-welfare-laws), [DTN](https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/ag/livestock/article/2026/11/09/farm-bill-competes-crowded-lame-duck)
- The EATS Act (118th Congress) and a 2024 farm bill Prop 12 fix also failed. The December 2024 extension had no fix. [Farms.com](https://farms.com/news/pork-producers-deeply-disappointed-in-senate-democrats-failure-to-address-california-prop-12-in-2024-farm-bill-220037.aspx)
- In short, 0 of about 4 attempts over roughly 12 years have succeeded.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on the Save Our Bacon Act, Prop 12 preemption, or 2026 farm bill passage.
- The markets supplied with this task are about the SAVE Act / SAVE America Act, a voter-ID bill (Kalshi 1% before January 4, 2027). They are unrelated and do not apply.
- Expert views are pessimistic about lame-duck farm bill passage at all (see the analyst quotes in section 3).

## 6. Upcoming events
- 2026-12-11: government funding deadline. An omnibus or CR is a possible farm bill vehicle. [DTN](https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/ag/livestock/article/2026/11/09/farm-bill-competes-crowded-lame-duck)
- 2026-12-18: scheduled adjournment. The 119th Congress ends 2027-01-03, and the pending bills die then. [Brownfield](https://brownfieldagnews.com/news/boozman-farm-bill-compromise-possible-during-lame-duck-session/)
- The NDAA conference is another possible vehicle in the lame duck.
- January 2027: the 120th Congress begins under Democratic control of both chambers and both Agriculture Committees. Any 2027 farm bill or appropriations bill would be written by Democratic majorities through the June 30, 2027 deadline.
- Watch for any compromise text, such as Ernst's. If it grandfathers existing laws like Prop 12 and Question 3, it would not resolve Yes.

Not found: I could not get an official congress.gov status page, and I found no November 2026 reporting of any active lame-duck negotiation over Save Our Bacon text specifically.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left and what Yes requires:** About 7.5 months remain, to July 1, 2027. Yes requires enactment of full preemption of state production-process standards for out-of-state pork. A grandfather clause, a prospective-only rule or a state opt-out would not count. Realistically, this must happen either in the lame duck, which ends around Dec 18, 2026, or under a Democratic-controlled 120th Congress in the first half of 2027.

**(b) Status quo:** No enactment. The House farm bill (H.R. 7567) has the language. The Senate committee bill does not. Both bills die on Jan 3, 2027.

**(c) Base rate:** King Amendment and EATS-style preemption has been attempted roughly four times since 2013. It has never been enacted, and each time it was dropped in conference or never moved. A lame-duck farm bill passed in 2018 after Democrats flipped the House, but without the King language. That gives a base rate of about 0 of 4, or roughly 5% per attempt even with generous smoothing, and lower given current conditions.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**
- **For Yes:**
  - Nov 6: Boozman says a lame-duck compromise is possible and lists Prop 12 as an open issue.
  - The Dec 11 funding deadline gives an omnibus as a possible vehicle.
  - NPPC is still pushing to keep the House language.
- **For No:**
  - Sep 16: the Senate Agriculture Committee passed its bill 12-11 without the language.
  - Boozman says not a single Democrat would vote for the House provision, and the Senate needs 60 votes.
  - The Ernst compromise grandfathers Prop 12, so it would not count even if enacted.
  - Nov 3: Democrats flipped both chambers, which removes their incentive to compromise.
  - Nov 9-10: analysts put farm bill odds at "slim to none," and Binder expects the farm bill to slip to 2027.
  - Schumer opposes the provision.

**(e) Scenarios:**
- **No:** The lame duck passes a CR or extension without a farm bill. Democrats write their own farm bill in 2027 with no preemption, or with no farm bill done by June. This is the dominant path.
- **Yes:** A year-end omnibus carries a negotiated farm bill. Democrats trade full Prop 12 preemption for SNAP concessions. Trump signs it before Jan 3.

**(f) Adjustment:** I start near the roughly 5% base rate and move down. The provision lacks any Democratic Senate support. Even the main compromise vehicle would resolve No. The lame-duck farm bill itself is unlikely. After January, a Democratic Congress would not pass it. Some residual chance remains for an omnibus surprise, so I land around 2%.

Probability: 2%
